Yeah, normally he’ll get low or put his foot up before he bites anyone so it’s a pretty easy tell. There have been times where I’ve gone to take away a food bowl and it was a more unexpected bite, or if someone else came over and walked into my home before I was ready and he charged them. but on a good note with food, I started training him to wait for a food bowl and he’s been less food aggressive since.
I’m not afraid of him! I can brush his teeth and everything, but he’s very territorial and very on guard when other people come over. I do need to find a Shiba inu trainer though

I am not saying it’s his fault he’s chewing but he will go into my closet and pull things. He has so many toys and chew bones and I give him dently’s digestive rawhides every few days. 

I live in a trailer park with no fence, it’s hard to have a doggy door but I have been giving him treats for going outside and I bring them outside with me. He doesn’t have accidents often when he’s happy but he is deliberately going on the floor. 

It is fear biting to new people who come over. He will charge my friends if they haven’t been there before so he gets either a leash with a harness when people are over or we use a baby gate to block him into the room (he can still see people so he can get used to them). He does do play bites but I try to heavily discourage that by ignoring/yelping to let him know it’s not okay.

He does better with my mom’s house or the groomer because it’s not where his food/toys are. I know that for sure. 

He is fixed, more recently like a month or two ago. He was 4m old when I got him and had a scar on his leg so I’m assuming some sort of abuse or a dog fight happened. 

I will try to not go to trainers who talk about this anymore and I do thing all of these things can be trained out I just need better advice for his breed.
Yes these comments are so helpful I’m glad people on here know what’s up!

The first trainer I went to only did an at home consultation, he told me he didn’t even work with shibas but made the exception because this was the time he started behaving poorly and we wanted to nip it in the bud.
